title: Blocked sites dataset: which websites are measurably blocked, by country and month
description:
Per-country, per-domain website reachability derived from OONI's public web_connectivity measurements, published as one CSV per month.

For each country and domain the dataset records how many tests ran, how many confirmed a block, how many were anomalous, how many reached the site normally, and how many failed. Confirmed and anomalous counts are separate columns and must never be added together: a confirmed block means censorship was positively identified, typically by a block page, while an anomaly means a connection failed in a way that censorship causes and so does an ordinary outage. Summing them inflates blocking figures, in some countries several-fold.

Countries need at least 1,000 measurements in the month and at least one confirmed block to appear; domains need at least 20 measurements in that country. Rows where nothing was blocked are kept deliberately, so that a domain absent from a country is unambiguously untested rather than possibly tested and reachable.

Known limits, stated because they matter for any reuse: the domains tested come largely from the Citizen Lab test lists and are curated rather than exhaustive, so absence is usually evidence of no test rather than of no block; OONI probes are run by volunteers and reflect the networks those volunteers are on, not a random sample; and a month is long enough that blocks starting or ending mid-month appear as partial rates.

The underlying measurements are OONI's and are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; this dataset is a derivative and carries the same terms. The code that builds it is MIT.
